questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities and to visit a new country.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A warm climate, far away from Europe, and the units the university offered.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the coordinator sent out information and the dorm I stayed at was also helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really need any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different types of housing. I lived in the Queen Mary Building but it was possible to apply to the Regiment and SCAPE as well.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my building there was a huge common kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Most exchange students live here so it is a great way of meeting other students, also because a lot of the social stuff happens here.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got an email telling me when and how to register, so it is very easy to do it. If I had any questions, the coordinator from University of Sydney was very helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a coordinator that I could contact.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Two of the courses I wanted was not open to exchange students but I got the ones I was able to apply to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have any questions, just ask the coordinator. Most of them are very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is a little bit easier at KU but much more work during the semester at USYD.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are mandatory work during the semester. It can be tests, assignments, quizes or mid-term exams, while at KU I am used to having one final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EDUH4058: Sport and Learning in Australian Culture
ENVI5707: Energy - Sources, Uses and Alternatives
GOVT6135: Global Environmental Politics
SUST5002: Food and Water Security

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend "Sport and Learning in Australian Culture" because you have very few lecture and a lot of fieldtrips to different sports games. Many exchange student take this course. I also recommend the other courses, they were all good and the professors are very engaging! My favorite was probably the energy or politics course.

How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: USYD has a lot of sports and social clubs to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Scuba diving club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to Western Australia and go south towards Esperance. Nicest beaches in Australia and there are not many people there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The best way to socializing with Australians is to talk to them in class because most of them leave campus right after the lecture. Or just go to a bar

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very open and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Travel around Australia as much as possible
- Join events at the start as this is how you meet other exchange students 
- Choose courses that doesn't have a final exam so you are done with your semester earlier and can travel more

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to meet so many nice and cool people, and being able to travel around Australia and Fiji with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to having to complete several quizzes, assignments, etc. during the semester and not only having one final exam at the end of the semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
